thread_tweets.text:
3️⃣ Open interest vs volume
Volume tells us how much was traded over a period, while open interest (OI) tells us the value of positions still open at a given moment.

A trader can open and close positions all day, adding to volume each time, but finish with no open position.

So @HyperliquidX’s lead here means it holds the largest share of open positions by value, but it doesn’t mean it has the most traders or that every market is easy to exit.

tweets.text:
DeFi has around $91B in TVL right now.

But how much of that money is actually protected if something goes wrong? The money set aside to cover losses is only about 0.14% of that.

We spend hours comparing vault APYs and strategies, but rarely check what happens if a protocol gets exploited. 

It’s like obsessing over a car’s horsepower and skipping the insurance.

DeFi already has protection options. The problem is that most vaults don't include them, leaving users to arrange to cover themselves.

Interestingly, @Firelightfi recently launched a different approach to this, where the vault operator sets up the cover so every depositor gets it automatically.

Here's how it works.

If a covered vault suffers an eligible exploit, five independent security firms review the incident against predefined terms. Once validated, eligible losses can be paid from the capital backing the cover, subject to coverage limits.

The money behind those payouts comes from people staking $FXRP, which is basically $XRP brought over to the Flare network. They earn rewards for taking on that risk, and there’s already 50M+ FXRP staked.

It’s live on Sentora’s USD and RWA vaults, and Veda and Upshift have plugged it in so vaults built on them can switch it on anytime.

I wouldn’t treat this as a guarantee. It only covers specific events like hacks and oracle attacks, and the terms still matter.

But having protection built into a vault, rather than making everyone arrange it separately is kinda how this should’ve worked from the start.

tweets.full_text:
DeFi has around $91B in TVL right now.

But how much of that money is actually protected if something goes wrong? The money set aside to cover losses is only about 0.14% of that.

We spend hours comparing vault APYs and strategies, but rarely check what happens if a protocol gets exploited. 

It’s like obsessing over a car’s horsepower and skipping the insurance.

DeFi already has protection options. The problem is that most vaults don't include them, leaving users to arrange to cover themselves.

Interestingly, @Firelightfi recently launched a different approach to this, where the vault operator sets up the cover so every depositor gets it automatically.

Here's how it works.

If a covered vault suffers an eligible exploit, five independent security firms review the incident against predefined terms. Once validated, eligible losses can be paid from the capital backing the cover, subject to coverage limits.

The money behind those payouts comes from people staking $FXRP, which is basically $XRP brought over to the Flare network. They earn rewards for taking on that risk, and there’s already 50M+ FXRP staked.

It’s live on Sentora’s USD and RWA vaults, and Veda and Upshift have plugged it in so vaults built on them can switch it on anytime.

I wouldn’t treat this as a guarantee. It only covers specific events like hacks and oracle attacks, and the terms still matter.

But having protection built into a vault, rather than making everyone arrange it separately is kinda how this should’ve worked from the start.

$1.3B in tokens unlocks in October. 

Here are the 5 I'm watching, and the 4 things that tell you whether an unlock actually dumps:

- $PUMP (Oct 11): ~$41.5M unlocking, around 1.5% of supply. Up roughly 12% over the 7 days after its previous unlock on Sep 11.

- $APT (Oct 11): ~$8.5M unlocking, around 0.6% of supply. After its previous unlock on Sep 11, APT fell roughly 7% over the next 7 days.

- $STRK (Oct 15): ~$6.2M unlocking, around 3.4% of supply. 

The ironic part? STRK gained roughly 73% in the 7 days after its Sep 14 unlock.

- $ARB (Oct 16): ~$17M unlocking, around 1.6% of supply. ARB was up roughly 69% in the week after its Sep 15 unlock.

- $ZRO (Oct 20): ~$54M unlocking, around 4% of supply. Its Sep 19 unlock was followed by roughly a 45% gain over the next 7 days.

The obvious mistake here would be looking at those September returns and assuming the same thing happens again.

A lot of that was the market. $BTC went from ~$63k in mid-August to the high $80s by Mid-September, sentiment flipped bullish, and alts caught the wave right as these unlocks were hitting.

The better question is what actually happens to the new tokens.

HYPE is the best example from this week. Its unlock looked huge on paper, but a large part of the team allocation being claimed was sold OTC to a single institutional buyer instead of immediately hitting the open market.

That’s why I’d care more about:

1. how big the unlock is vs supply
2. who receives it
3. whether those tokens move to exchanges
4. what the market is doing at the same time

For most of these, the tokens go to the team, core contributors, and strategic partners, so that part doesn't separate them much. Size does, which is why $ZRO and $STRK get most of my attention at 4% and 3.4% of supply.

Which upcoming unlock are you watching most closely?

Friedberg: “We're watching the birth of a new religion.”

“The idea that you can prescribe or describe AI as being conscious is effectively the creation of a new belief system, a system that doesn't actually spread via proof, it spreads via narrative.

‘Please believe it with me. Here's why I think we should believe this thing together.’

It's not based on evidence, it’s not based on data, it's not provable.

Over time, what happens is some set of people believe this thing, and they form a group. And in some cases, that group is known as a religion. And that new belief system creates new power structures, which is now, ‘Our view is different than your view, and we want to have more people on our side with our view. And therefore we have to try and create leverage and create power with our system.’

I think that if we fast-forward a couple of years, there's going to be large groups of people on Earth that are gonna believe that AI is conscious, and there are going to be large groups of people that believe that AI is not conscious.

And those groups will come into conflict, fighting over control of the AI, or allowing the AI to do things or not do things, or who gets to use the AI, or who gets to be in charge of the AI. And it will very likely lead to human to human conflict.

I know that that's a very far and deep extrapolation of where we are, but I think that the fact that we are seeing (Anthropic) go and meet with religious leaders today to try and get them to believe in this new belief system plants the seed.

And it's not just anyone doing this, it is the most powerful AI lab on Earth.

And you can see in the Claude usage policy that was just published, it says, ‘You are not allowed to engage in sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior toward our models.’

There is an anthropomorphizing conditioning going on with all of us where we talk about models as if they are a thing. One way to describe this is a software program is writing text on a screen that tells the user, ‘I am a thing.’”

Having spent 10 years building AI products, this resonates a lot.

Machine learning has long been a black box. Now we’re giving a much more capable black box access to our most sensitive data and the ability to act on our behalf.

Alignment is still a huge challenge. We may never fully understand why a model made a particular decision or which training data shaped it. We need guardrails around it that hold even when the model gets things wrong.

An email agent can have read-only access: it can summarize your inbox, but it has no permission to send anything. Through Entra ID, an agent acting on your behalf stays within explicitly granted permissions and your existing access.

These boundaries need to be enforced outside the model. Same for action logs, spending limits and the ability to stop it mid-task.

“Don’t do this” in a prompt is a request. Removing the permission is a control.

Having spent 10 years building AI products, this resonates a lot.

Machine learning has long been a black box. Now we’re giving a much more capable black box access to our most sensitive data and the ability to act on our behalf.

Alignment is still a huge challenge. We may never fully understand why a model made a particular decision or which training data shaped it. We need guardrails around it that hold even when the model gets things wrong.

An email agent can have read-only access: it can summarize your inbox, but it has no permission to send anything. Through Entra ID, an agent acting on your behalf stays within explicitly granted permissions and your existing access.

These boundaries need to be enforced outside the model. Same for action logs, spending limits and the ability to stop it mid-task.

“Don’t do this” in a prompt is a request. Removing the permission is a control.

This is everything I admired about America as a teenager growing up in France.

Michael Dell starts a company at 19 in his dorm room with $1,000, becomes a billionaire, then he and Susan commit $6.25 billion to give 25 million American children their first investment.

I remember my high school teachers blaming large corporations and their dividends. It was just accepted in the classroom: corporations were evil, dividends were evil.

And I remember thinking: wait. There’s a system where I can buy a piece of these companies, and they’ll give me money on a recurring basis?

Everyone was explaining why this was terrible, and all I could think was: I need a piece of that. If I want to escape poverty, I need to own some of these businesses.

It took me years to understand investing properly. I hope these kids get that realization much sooner.

Munger said: “Show me the incentive and I’ll show you the outcome.”

You can explain the benefits of capitalism forever. But owning a piece of a business gives you a personal reason to understand profits, dividends, reinvestment and compounding.

Suddenly, America’s most successful companies are partly yours. Their success means something to you.

And maybe a kid who starts by asking “What do I own?” will eventually ask “What could I build?”

That’s what makes this so inspiring to me. A man who built his fortune giving millions of children a first experience of ownership, and perhaps the ambition to build something themselves.

This is the America I dreamed of.
LFG America 🇺🇸
